metadata.methods_description: Seven healthy adults (ages 20–30 years) completed nine sessions of EEG-based brain-machine interface training and closed-loop exoskeleton control. Each session consisted of a motor imagery calibration phase followed by 12 closed-loop trials with walk/stop conditions. Extended motor imagery tasks (6-minute walk and stop imagery) were performed after trial blocks. Data acquisition included 60-channel scalp EEG with 4 EOG channels, 3-axis IMU sensors mounted on the forehead and exoskeleton, and continuous logging of decoder signals and BMI feedback.
